system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
diagnosis: Use of the teach-back method to confirm patient understanding
mechanism: Teach-back checks the clarity of clinician communication by asking the patient to explain in their own words what they need to know or do; it is framed as a test of the clinician's explanation rather than a test of the patient's memory and should be repeated after clarification if misunderstanding is identified.
vignette: A patient with newly diagnosed heart failure is being discharged with several medication changes, daily weight monitoring, and instructions about when to seek urgent care. After counseling, the patient nods and says, 'Yes, I understand.' The physician wants to verify that the instructions were communicated clearly.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
correct: Ask the patient to explain in their own words how they will follow the plan, framing the request as a check of how clearly the physician explained it
distractors: Ask the patient, 'Do you understand everything I just explained?'
Repeat the same instructions once more and assume comprehension if the patient does not ask questions
Give the patient a written handout and defer any further assessment of understanding
Ask the patient to recite the instructions word-for-word without referring to any written materials
distractor_notes: Yes/no questions such as 'Do you understand?' do not reliably demonstrate comprehension and are specifically discouraged as teach-back questions.
Repeating information without asking the patient to demonstrate understanding does not verify whether communication was effective.
Written materials can reinforce counseling but do not replace active confirmation that the patient understands what to do.
Teach-back asks for the plan in the patient's own words and is not a memory test or verbatim recitation exercise.
key_expl: Teach-back is an evidence-based health-literacy technique in which the clinician asks the patient to explain the plan in their own words. The request should be nonshaming and should place responsibility on the clinician's explanation. If misunderstanding is found, the clinician clarifies and checks again.
objective: Use teach-back to verify comprehension by asking patients to explain care instructions in their own words rather than relying on yes/no confirmation or passive written materials.
clues: patient says yes without demonstrating comprehension
